items.title: The degenerate affine Hecke algebra
items.statement: For d≥0 the degenerate affine Hecke algebra H_d has commuting polynomial generators x_1,…,x_d and the symmetric-group generators s_i, with s_i x_j=x_j s_i outside j=i,i+1 and s_i x_(i+1)=x_i s_i+1, x_(i+1)s_i=s_i x_i+1. Its ordered monomials x_1^r1…x_d^rd w, r_i≥0 and w∈S_d, form a basis. Thus H_0=C and H_1=C[x_1]. The evaluation H_d/(x_1−a)≅C[S_d] sends x_j to a+sum_(k<j)(k j), not to the same scalar for every j. Polynomial degree gives a filtration with gr H_d=C[x_1,…,x_d] semidirect C[S_d]; the inhomogeneous cross relation is not a grading with deg x=1, deg s=0.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Move polynomial generators left using the cross relations; braid and commutation resolve the overlaps. For independence act on rational functions with s_i=permutation_i−(x_i−x_(i+1))^−1(1−permutation_i). The coefficient of each distinct rational-function permutation is triangular with invertible diagonal, so the monomials are independent. Verify the cross and braid identities by clearing denominators in two/three adjacent variables. The Jucys sums satisfy the same relations and the quotient recursion identifies every x_j, giving evaluation. This is the explicit rational-operator proof in the affine-Yangian local note §1.

items.title: Type-A nilpotent orbit closures are normal via chain varieties
items.statement: Assume AC and let e be a nilpotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex vector space V. The closure X of its GL(V)-conjugacy orbit has a reduced irreducible NORMAL coordinate domain. The orbit boundary has codimension at least2. This holds for every Jordan type, not only the regular nilpotent cone. A complete proof uses the auxiliary chain equations B_1A_1=0 and B_iA_i=A_(i−1)B_(i−1): their actual scheme is a complete intersection, smooth outside a codimension≥2 subset, reduced/irreducible/normal, and its internal-vertex GL invariant ring is C[X].
items.strategy:
Complete local construction and proof in owner-category-o-batch17-vust-local-proof.md §§2–4. ## 2. Auxiliary chain variety and local rank calculation

For the Jordan partition η of e let t=l, q_1≥...≥q_t>0 its column lengths. Put n_i=q_t+...+q_{t-i+1}, 1≤i≤t, n_0=0, U_i=C^{n_i}. Let
M=product_{i=1}^{t-1}(Hom(U_i,U_{i+1})×Hom(U_{i+1},U_i)).
Write its coordinates (A_i,B_i), and let Z be the actual scheme cut out by
B_1A_1=0, B_iA_i=A_{i-1}B_{i-1} (2≤i<t).
There are c=sum_{i<t}n_i² equations. On Z° where each A_i is injective OR B_i surjective, the differential of these equations is onto: at each stage solve Y_i A_i+B_i X_i=the prescribed residual, using a left inverse of A_i or right inverse of B_i, successively after the earlier variables have been chosen. The actual nonradical Jacobian supplier therefore gives smoothness and dimension D=2sum_{i<t}n_i n_{i+1}−sum_{i<t}n_i² there.

This open set is nonempty. Take U_{t-k}=im(e^k), with inclusions A_i and restrictions B_i=e. Both maps have maximal rank and satisfy the equations. The end map θ=A_{t-1}B_{t-1} has typeη. For t=1 take Z=Spec C, θ=0 and H trivial; the zero orbit is normal directly.

## 3. Complete ab-string dimension and boundary estimate

A nilpotent pair A:U→V,B:V→U is the odd nilpotent operator T on U⊕V. The usual Jordan string construction can be made homogeneous: kernels, images and all successive quotient spaces are Z/2-graded, so choose homogeneous complements/bases at every stage. Its indecomposables are alternating a/b strings. Suppressing the b letters gives the Jordan diagram of BA, suppressing a gives that of AB. This proves the classification and finiteness without a quiver-classification theorem. Injectivity/surjectivity are read from the first/last letters; in the relevant dimU≤dimV case, A injective means every string ends in b, B surjective means every string starts in b.

Let r_j,s_j be the numbers of a,b letters in each string, and let a_k,b_k count odd strings of lengthk starting respectively with a,b. Put Delta=sum_{k odd}a_k b_k. A graded Hom between strings has min(L_i,L_j) possible shifts. For both odd lengths the difference of even/odd Hom dimensions is the product of their endpoint signs. For an odd/even pair the two opposite Hom directions cancel that difference; for two even lengths it is0. Hence the superdimension of the full centralizer is (dimU−dimV)². Subtracting the even centralizer dimension from dimGL(U)×GL(V) proves that the pair orbit has half the dimension of the full GL(U⊕V) nilpotent orbit, rather than importing this half-dimension fact.

Also
min(r_i+s_i,r_j+s_j)=min(r_i,r_j)+min(s_i,s_j)
except for equal odd lengths of opposite endpoint signs, when it is larger by1. Summing ordered pairs gives the correction2Delta. The ordinary Jordan centralizer has dimension sum_{i,j}min(L_i,L_j), since a module map between C[t]/t^{L_i} and C[t]/t^{L_j} has that dimension. Therefore, if the pair orbit projects to ordinary orbits C_alpha,C_beta,
dim X_delta=dimU dimV+(dim C_alpha+dim C_beta)/2−Delta.
All stabilizers here are unit groups of finite-dimensional even endomorphism algebras, principal opens in vector spaces, hence smooth connected irreducible in characteristic zero.

Stratify Z by the finite compatible sequences of these pair diagrams. The pair-orbit maps to their ordinary nilpotent orbits are locally trivial smooth maps with irreducible fibers: locally choose Jordan bases by fixed nonzero rank minors; their stabilizer fibers are quotients of the connected centralizer unit groups just described. Iterating these fiber products proves that each stratum Z_lambda is smooth irreducible and
 dim Z_lambda=sum_{i<t}n_i n_{i+1}+dim C_sigma/2−sum_i Delta_i,
where sigma is the final end-map type. Powers of the end map factor through U_{t-k}, so rank θ^k≤n_{t-k}. Thus sigma is dominated byη (equivalently the conjugate-partition partial-sum rank inequalities). The ordinary orbit formula is N²−sum_j q_j², or N²−sum_i(2i−1)η_i. It implies every distinct dominated type has dimension smaller by an even positive integer.

There is exactly one stratum over typeη: each final b-diagram must be filled internally with the n_{t-1} a letters; there are exactly that many, so every row starts and ends in b. Removing the first column repeats this argument inductively. This stratum lies in Z° and has dimensionD. If the final orbit dimension drops by at least4, the displayed stratum formula already gives dim≤D−2.

For a drop exactly2, the prefix-sum expression for orbit dimension shows that exactly one prefix drops by1, so the diagram moves a box to the NEXT row. Analyze one link and remove the first column. If the receiving row was nonempty, the internal filling uses all available a's and every row starts/ends in b; the lower a-diagram is again this one-box degeneration. If a new one-box row is created, exactly one a remains after internal filling. The condition that the a-diagram be dominated by the prescribed diagram with its first column removed permits it only at either end of the last shortened b-row, at either end of the new b-row, or as a separate a-row. The first four placements make A or B maximal rank and either remove the degeneration or pass it down. The separate a-row makes both maps nonmaximal and contributes Delta_i≥1 (there is an a-only and at least one b-only row; for shortened length1 there can be two b-only rows, so equality1 need not be asserted). Induction down the links proves: every stratum outside Z° has dim≤D−2. This is the full two-case/five-placement argument of KP5.4–5.6, including the short-string corner, not a nominal dimension estimate.

## 4. Complete intersection, normality and the actual invariant quotient

The previous estimate gives dimZ=D and no lower-dimensional component: every component of a scheme cut out by c equations has dimension≥dimM−c=D, while the complement strata have smaller dimension. Thus the c generators have heightc. In the polynomial Cohen–Macaulay ambient ring they form a regular sequence: localize at the homogeneous maximal ideal, use the height bound for each prefix (Krull height gives height(prefix)≥c−remaining=k), extend to a system of parameters and apply the actual CM parameter theorem. Homogeneous localization detects failure of injectivity, so this is global. The quotient is CM, hence S2/S1; it is generically smooth R0. The actual R0+S1 reducedness lemma makes it reduced. The unique irreducible D-dimensional stratum over typeη is dense: every other stratum has smaller dimension, while every component has dimensionD, so a second component would have a nonempty D-dimensional open subset outside that first closure, impossible. Thus the reduced quotient is a domain. Regularity in codimension1 plus S2 now makes this domain normal by the actual Serre criterion. This proves irreducibility before using a domain-only normality supplier. This avoids assuming reducedness before applying the nonradical Jacobian clause.

Let H=product_{i<t}GL(U_i). We prove, rather than quote, that C[Z]^H is generated by the entries of θ. First, for Hom(U,V)×Hom(V,U), polynomial invariants under GL(U) are generated by entries of AB. Scalar weights force equal degrees in A,B; polarize and apply the actual Schur–Weyl centralizer to U^⊗k, whose invariant contractions pair each U with a U* in a permutation. Depolarization gives products of AB entries. No general invariant-theory FFT is imported.

Invariants of a rational polynomial quotient lift. Every vector lies in a finite-dimensional stable subspace (bounded polynomial degree); its scalar torus acts diagonally by integral degree weights. The actual Weyl theorem splits the derived sl modules inside each torus weight. Thus finite-degree rational GL modules are completely reducible and invariant quotient vectors have invariant lifts; integration is checked on elementary unipotents and diagonal matrices, which generate GL. This works also for the needed finite-dimensional coefficient modules. Apply this exact invariant lifting successively at vertices1,...,t−1. At the first vertex the invariant generators are A_1B_1 and all remaining matrix entries; on Z the former equal B_2A_2, so they can be eliminated. Continue, leaving only θ's matrix entries. Consequently C[Z]^H is precisely the coordinate ring of the closure of θ(Z). The unique dense stratum maps onto the conjugacy orbit of e (all Jordan bases are covered), so that closure is its orbit closure.

The invariant subring of a normal domain is normal: an element of Frac(C[Z]^H) integral over that subring is integral over C[Z], hence in C[Z], and remains H-fixed. Thus the desired nilpotent orbit closure has a normal coordinate domain. All its boundary orbits have smaller even dimension by the finite Jordan classification and the orbit formula; the boundary therefore has codimension≥2. Neither rational singularities nor Hochster–Roberts is needed.

items.title: Arakawa-Suzuki Casimir operators on the tensor functors
items.statement: For gl_N with trace Casimir Ω=sum E_ij tensor E_ji, on M tensor V^tensor d put x_j=Ω_0j+sum_(k<j)P_kj and s_i=P_(i,i+1). Equivalently x_(j+1)=s_j x_j s_j+s_j; these operators are natural and commute with gl_N. For the sl_N Arakawa–Suzuki normalization, if z=sum E_ii acts on M by z_M, the source generators are y_j=x_j−z_M/N+(N−1)/2 and its transpositions are the same P. The sl_N Casimir is Ω_gl−z tensor z/N. Degree zero omits all x_j. Trivial M gives x_j=sum_(k<j)P_kj, with x_1=0.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Expand the trace dual basis and observe Ω on V tensor V is the flip. Subtract the scalar central summand to pass to sl_N: Ω_0j loses z_M/N, while each Ω_kj loses1/N, which the source's added1/N restores. Its remaining shift is (N−1)/2. Read and compare the actual AS2.2.2, rather than identify x and y without this scalar. The universal formulas make naturality and the recursion immediate.

items.title: Nilpotent-orbit tensor covariants extend and polarize
items.statement: Assume AC, e∈End_C(V) nilpotent and d≥0. Every G_e-fixed B∈End_C(V^⊗d) is the value at e of a GL(V)-equivariant POLYNOMIAL tensor covariant Phi:End(V)→End(V^⊗d). Every such Phi is a sum, with invariant scalar polynomial coefficients, of X↦sigma composed with X^h1⊗...⊗X^hd. The extension is proved on the normal codimension-two orbit closure and lifted using finite rational GL complete reducibility; the covariant formula is proved by polarization and Schur–Weyl permutation contractions, not an imported Procesi FFT.
items.strategy:
Complete local argument in owner-category-o-batch17-vust-local-proof.md §5. ## 5. Extension and polarized tensor covariants

Let X be this normal orbit closure and O its dense orbit. Regular functions on O extend to X. Here is the needed Hartogs argument without an imported intersection theorem. For f∈Frac A regular off codimension≥2, put J={a∈A:af∈A}. At every height-one prime J is the unit ideal. If J were proper choose0≠a∈J. In the normal S2 domain every associated prime of A/(a) has height1, by localization, the actual depth-zero criterion and the regular-element depth shift. Finite prime avoidance supplies b∈J avoiding those primes. Since b(af)=a(bf), regularity of b modulo a implies af∈aA. Cancellation gives f∈A, contradiction. Apply coordinatewise to maps into a finite-dimensional vector representation.

For B∈End(V^⊗d) fixed by G_e, define on O the equivariant map g e g^{-1}↦g^⊗d B(g^{-1})^⊗d. It is well-defined. It is regular: on rank-minor charts of the constant-rank powers choose bases of kerX^k, their image/quotient complements and hence homogeneous Jordan top vectors by Gaussian elimination. The resulting Jordan-basis conjugator g(X) and its inverse are regular where the finitely many chosen minors/determinant do not vanish. These charts coverO and the expressions agree by G_e-invariance. Hartogs extends the map equivariantly to X (equality on the dense orbit gives equality everywhere). Finite-degree GL complete reducibility then lifts it to an equivariant polynomial map Phi:End(V)→End(V^⊗d).

To determine Phi, polarize its degree-k matrix input and pair its output with d independent matrices Y_1,...,Y_d by the nondegenerate trace form. This is a multilinear invariant on End(V)^{k+d}; the actual Schur–Weyl theorem identifies all such invariants with permutation contractions. Each permutation gives products of traces along its cycles, by expansion of matrix indices. Depolarizing the k identical X variables leaves cycles consisting only of X (scalar invariant coefficients) and cycles through the Y's, of the form Tr(X^{a_1}Y_{i_1}...X^{a_r}Y_{i_r}). These latter cycles are exactly the trace pairing of Y_1⊗...⊗Y_d with a place permutation followed by X^{h_1}⊗...⊗X^{h_d}. Nondegeneracy of trace therefore proves that Phi is a sum of these operator covariants with scalar invariant polynomial coefficients. Evaluating at e gives only permutation×individual e powers; powers≥l vanish. This proves the FULL converse centralizer identity for every nilpotent type and every d, independently of stable faithfulness.

items.title: The type-A nilpotent pyramid, good grading and Whittaker character
items.statement: Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a partition of $N$ with transpose $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l\ge0$ and let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$. Number the boxes of the diagram of $\lambda$ by $1,\dots,N$ down columns from the left, write $\mathrm{row}(i),\mathrm{col}(i)$ for the row and column of the $i$-th box, let $L(i)$ and $R(i)$ be the numbers of its immediate left and right neighbours (or $\emptyset$ if absent), and define the nilpotent $e=\sum_{i:L(i)\ne\emptyset}e_{L(i),i}\in\mathfrak g$, $v_i\mapsto v_{L(i)}$. Declare $\deg e_{i,j}=\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i)$ and let $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbb Z}\mathfrak g_r$, $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$, $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak g_0$, $\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r$. Then $e\in\mathfrak g_1$ has Jordan type $\lambda$ (largest Jordan block $l$), $\mathfrak p$ is a parabolic subalgebra with Levi factor $\mathfrak h\cong\mathfrak{gl}_{q_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{q_l}$ and nilradical $\bigoplus_{r>0}\mathfrak g_r$, $\mathfrak m$ is the nilradical of the opposite parabolic, $\mathfrak g^{e}$ is the graded subalgebra $\bigoplus_{r\ge0}(\mathfrak g_r\cap\mathfrak g^e)$ generated by the elements $e_{i,j;r}=\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{row}(h)=i,\mathrm{row}(k)=j\\ \mathrm{col}(k)-\mathrm{col}(h)=r}}e_{h,k}$ for $s_{i,j}\le r<p_j$ (where $s_{i,j}=p_j-p_i$ for $i\le j$ and $s_{i,j}=0$ for $i\ge j$), Put $I_{box}=\{1,\ldots,N\}$, $J=\{(a,b)\in I_{box}^2:\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b),\ R(b)=\emptyset\}$ and $K=\{(i,j,r):1\le i,j\le n,\ s_{i,j}\le r<p_j\}$. The map $(a,b)\mapsto(\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b),\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a))$ is a bijection $J\to K$. Its inverse takes $b$ to the rightmost box of row $j$ and $a$ to the box in row $i$ at column $p_j-r$. The finite sum $\xi_{a,b}=\sum_{t=0}^{\mathrm{col}(a)-1}e_{L^t(a),L^t(b)}$ equals $e_{\mathrm{row}(a),\mathrm{row}(b);\mathrm{col}(b)-\mathrm{col}(a)}$; these elements for $(a,b)\in J$ form the same basis of $\mathfrak g^e$ as the elements indexed by $K$. Finally set $\chi(x)=(x,e)=\mathrm{tr}(xe)$ for $x\in\mathfrak m$; then $\chi$ is a Lie algebra character, i.e. $\chi([\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m])=0$. This grading is the type-A pyramid good grading, not the Dynkin grading of an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple; it is the one used for the finite W-algebra of the higher-level Schur-Weyl duality.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Check [E_ab,E_cd]=delta_bc E_ad−delta_ad E_cb and e v_i=v_L(i). Each row is one Jordan string. For Hom between strings of lengths p_a,p_b, the sl2 decomposition has top grading2(p_b−k)≥0 and bottom−2(p_a−k)≤0, 1≤k≤min(p_a,p_b), under the doubled grading. This proves injectivity/surjectivity of ad e in the negative/nonnegative degrees and the stated centralizer basis, rather than importing the Dynkin grading. The column blocks give the parabolic and opposite radical. Since brackets of negative degrees have degree≤−2 while e has degree1, trace([m,m]e)=0. The undoubled source grading has e degree1; its doubled version has no odd degrees and e degree2. For fixed row labels i,j, the right endpoint b has column p_j. Requiring a at column p_j−r to exist in row i is exactly max(0,p_j−p_i)≤r<p_j, the declared K range. This proves the bijection with J. Successive left shifts terminate after col(a) terms, give every row-pair matrix unit of the same displacement, and commute with e by cancellation of adjacent summands and the right-end boundary. The string calculation gives min(p_i,p_j) independent maps per row pair, so these finite sums are the full centralizer basis. The loop consumers use (i,j,r)∈K and T^(r+1), without confusing box and row indices.

items.title: The Casimir and place-permutation operators satisfy the degenerate affine Hecke relations
items.statement: For every gl_N-module M, these x_j and place permutations give a natural commuting right H_d action on M tensor V^tensor d, using the generator-fixing anti-involution to encode right actions. All Coxeter, polynomial commutation and affine cross relations hold. In particular the x_i commute; this is an essential additional check, not a consequence of the permutation braid alone.
items.strategy:
**Given:** $N\ge1$, a $\mathfrak g$-module $M$ with $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$, the natural module $V$, $d\ge0$, and the operators of [[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]] built from the trace-form Casimir $\Omega=\sum_{i,j}E_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}$.

[F1] The operators $P_{ab}$ are the place permutations of the labelled tensor factors; $P_{ab}^2=1$, and $P_{ab}$ commutes with $P_{cd}$ when $\{a,b\}\cap\{c,d\}=\varnothing$ ([[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]], [[thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products]]).

[F2] On two natural factors $\Omega_{ij}=P_{ij}$; more generally, for any triple of factors $a,b,c$ the element identity $[\Omega_{ab},\Omega_{ac}+\Omega_{bc}]=0$ holds in $U(\mathfrak g)^{\otimes3}$, and $[\Omega_{ab},P_{cd}]=0$ whenever the pairs of labels are disjoint ([[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]], [[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]).

[F3] $[E_{ab},E_{cd}]=\delta_{bc}E_{ad}-\delta_{ad}E_{cb}$ in $\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]).

[F4] The Hecke algebra $H_d$ is presented by the Coxeter relations for the $s_i$ and the cross relations $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$, $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$, together with $x_ix_j=x_jx_i$; the generator-fixing anti-involution $\omega$ of $H_d$ is the anti-automorphism fixing all generators, and a left action $\rho$ of $H_d$ defines a right action by $e\cdot u=\rho(\omega(u))e$ ([[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]).

[F5] The Casimir operator acts as an intertwiner and commutes with the $\mathfrak g$-action; place permutations of natural factors also commute with the $\mathfrak g$-action because the comultiplication is cocommutative ([[lem-the-casimir-operator-is-basis-independent-and-intertwining]], [[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The operators $x_j=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{k<j}P_{kj}$ and $s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, and the identities of [F1]-[F5].

1.1 The infinitesimal braid identities. For distinct labels $a,b,c$ one has $[\Omega_{ab},\Omega_{ac}+\Omega_{bc}]=0$: expanding $\Omega=\sum E_{uv}\otimes E_{vu}$ and using [F3], the double commutator sum splits into terms $[E_{uv},E_{xy}]\otimes E_{vu}\otimes E_{yx}$ and $E_{uv}\otimes[E_{vu},E_{xy}]\otimes E_{yx}$, and the two resulting sums cancel term by term after relabelling; equivalently, this is the identity $[\Omega_{12},\Omega_{13}+\Omega_{23}]=0$ in $U(\mathfrak g)^{\otimes3}$, which is the derivative of the invariance of $\Omega$ under the diagonal adjoint action. Consequently $[\Omega_{ab},\Omega_{ac}]=-[\Omega_{ab},\Omega_{bc}]=[\Omega_{ac},\Omega_{bc}]$. In particular, for three natural factors this is the identity $[P_{ab},P_{ac}]+[P_{ab},P_{bc}]=0$ for the flips. [F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 The Coxeter relations for $s_i$. $s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ is an involution; $s_is_j=s_js_i$ for $|i-j|>1$ because the pairs of interchanged labels are disjoint; and $s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1}$ because both sides are the permutation operator inducing the same permutation of the three labelled factors. [F1, algebra]

2.1 Cross relations. Conjugation by $s_i=P_{i,i+1}$ interchanges the labels $i$ and $i+1$ in any operator supported on those factors, so $s_i\Omega_{0,i+1}=\Omega_{0i}s_i$ and $s_iP_{k,i+1}=P_{ki}s_i$ for $k<i$. Therefore $s_ix_{i+1}=s_i\Omega_{0,i+1}+\sum_{k<i}s_iP_{k,i+1}+s_iP_{i,i+1}=\Omega_{0i}s_i+\sum_{k<i}P_{ki}s_i+1=x_is_i+1$, and symmetrically $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$. For $j<i$, all labels in $x_j$ are disjoint from $\{i,i+1\}$, so $s_i$ commutes with every summand. For $j>i+1$, $\Omega_{0j}$ and the terms $P_{kj}$ with $k\notin\{i,i+1\}$ commute with $s_i$, while conjugation by $s_i$ interchanges $P_{ij}$ and $P_{i+1,j}$. Their sum is invariant, so again $s_ix_j=x_js_i$; the two overlapping summands need not commute individually. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Polynomial commutation. Fix $i<j$. Since $x_i=\Omega_{0i}+\sum_{k<i}P_{ki}$ and $x_j=\Omega_{0j}+\sum_{l<j}P_{lj}$, the commutator is $[\Omega_{0i},\Omega_{0j}]+\sum_{l<j}[\Omega_{0i},P_{lj}]+\sum_{k<i}[P_{ki},\Omega_{0j}]+\sum_{k<i}\sum_{l<j}[P_{ki},P_{lj}]$. The second sum reduces to the single term $[\Omega_{0i},P_{ij}]$ (all other $P_{lj}$ are disjoint from the labels $0,i$), and the third sum vanishes (all pairs $\{k,i\}$, $\{0,j\}$ are disjoint since $k<i<j$). In the fourth sum only the terms with $k=l$ or $l=i$ can fail to vanish, so it equals $\sum_{k<i}([P_{ki},P_{kj}]+[P_{ki},P_{ij}])$. Hence $[x_i,x_j]=([\Omega_{0i},\Omega_{0j}]+[\Omega_{0i},P_{ij}])+\sum_{k<i}([P_{ki},P_{kj}]+[P_{ki},P_{ij}])$. The first bracket vanishes by step 1.1 with $a=0$, $b=i$, $c=j$ together with $\Omega_{ij}=P_{ij}$; each summand of the second bracket vanishes by step 1.1 for the three distinct labels $k,i,j$. Therefore $[x_i,x_j]=0$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Naturality, commutation with $\mathfrak g$, and the right action. The place permutations are natural in $M$ and commute with $\mathfrak g$; the Casimir operators are intertwiners by [F5]; hence every $x_j$ and $s_i$ is natural and $\mathfrak g$-linear. The relations established in steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 are exactly the defining relations of $H_d$ [F4], so the assignment $x_j\mapsto x_j$, $s_i\mapsto s_i$ defines a left $H_d$-action. The generator-fixing anti-automorphism $\omega$ of $H_d$ (which preserves each defining relation because the reversed cross relation $x_{i+1}s_i=s_ix_i+1$ is also a defining relation) converts it into a right action by $e\cdot u:=\rho(\omega(u))e$; the anti-automorphism property gives $(e\cdot u)\cdot v=\rho(\omega(v))\rho(\omega(u))e=\rho(\omega(uv))e=e\cdot(uv)$. This proves both assertions. [F4, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

## Remarks

- The two cross relations are not symmetric consequences of the braid relation: the summand $+s_i$ has no counterpart in the Coxeter presentation of $S_d$, and it is exactly the term responsible for the inhomogeneous filtration discussed in [[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]].

- The computation of step 2.2 uses $\Omega_{ij}=P_{ij}$ only on pairs of natural factors; the identities involving the module label $0$ are the universal commutation identities of the Casimir element and hold for arbitrary $M$.

items.title: The type-A finite W-algebra and the Whittaker category
items.statement: Keep the type-A pyramid data $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$ of the preceding item and let $\eta\colon U(\mathfrak p)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ be the algebra automorphism with $\eta(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}(n-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-q_{\mathrm{col}(j)+1}-\cdots-q_l)$ for all $e_{i,j}\in\mathfrak p$. Let $I_\chi$ be the kernel of the algebra homomorphism $\chi\colon U(\mathfrak m)\to\mathbb C$ extending the Lie character of the preceding item (so $I_\chi$ is the two-sided ideal generated by $x-\chi(x)$, $x\in\mathfrak m$) and let $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ be the left ideal it generates. The type-A finite W-algebra is $W(\lambda)=\{u\in U(\mathfrak p): [x,\eta(u)]\in U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi\ \text{for all } x\in\mathfrak m\}$; it is a subalgebra of $U(\mathfrak p)$, and $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a $(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule (the right action by $u\cdot\bar v=\overline{v\eta(u)}$). The Whittaker category $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ is the category of $\mathfrak g$-modules on which $x-\chi(x)$ acts locally nilpotently for every $x\in\mathfrak m$; for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the Whittaker vectors $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=\{v\in M: xv=\chi(x)v\ \forall x\in\mathfrak m\}$ form a $W(\lambda)$-module with $u\cdot v=\eta(u)v$, and $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$. The associated graded of the loop filtration on $U(\mathfrak p)$ makes $W(\lambda)$ a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ (proved below): this is the loop or good filtration, not the Kazhdan filtration.
items.strategy: Show closedness of $W(\lambda)$ under multiplication and $\eta$-equivariance of the defining condition; the bimodule structure on $Q_\chi$ follows because $W(\lambda)$ preserves the left ideal $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ by definition. The $W(\lambda)$-module structure on $\mathrm{Wh}(M)$ follows from $[\mathfrak m,\eta(W(\lambda))]\subseteq U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$: for $m\in\mathfrak m$, $u\in W(\lambda)$ and a Whittaker vector $v$ one has $m(\eta(u)v)=\eta(u)mv+[m,\eta(u)]v=\chi(m)\eta(u)v$. The vanishing statement $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0\Rightarrow M=0$ is proved by the Gan-Ginzburg/Skryabin cohomology argument in the next-but-one item; record it here as part of the categorical interface. The dictionary $\eta$ is the type-A $\rho$-shift of [BKHL, Introduction] and is the one used (with the automorphism $\eta_c$) on tensor space.

items.statement: Assume AC. For d≥0 and e with largest Jordan string lengthl≥1 let B=C[x_1,...,x_d]/(x_1^l,...,x_d^l) semidirect C[S_d], with individual x_i=e and place permutations on E=V^⊗d. Let phi:U(g^e)→End(E) be the diagonal representation and psi:B→End(E)^op the homomorphism encoding the right action. Then phi(U(g^e))=End_B(E) and End_g^e(E)^op=psi(B), for EVERY nilpotent Jordan type and EVERY d. The right action is injective if e has at leastd strings of maximum lengthl. For d=0 the identities and injectivity are scalar identities. The full converse uses the preceding proved normality/extension/tensor-covariant suppliers; it is not an assumed double-commutant inheritance or a stable-only claim.
items.strategy:
Complete local proof in owner-category-o-batch17-vust-local-proof.md §§1–5. ## 1. First centralizer and stable faithfulness, independent of normality

Let V be finite-dimensional over C, e nilpotent with largest string length l≥1, E=V^⊗d and B=C[x_1,...,x_d]/(x_1^l,...,x_d^l)⋊C[S_d], acting by individual e operators and places. Put A=End_{C[e]}V=g^e as an associative vector algebra. Under End(E)=End(V)^⊗d, commuting with each e in its individual position gives A^⊗d: choose complements to the kernels of [e,-] in the individual End(V) factors and compare the direct tensor summands. Commuting with place permutations then gives (A^⊗d)^{S_d}, the span of a^⊗d for a∈A by ordinary characteristic-zero polarization.

This span equals the image of U(g^e). One inclusion is immediate from commuting individual e/operators and places. For the other put a_i=1⊗...⊗a⊗...⊗1; these d operators commute. Newton identities express a_1...a_d as a polynomial over Q in their power sums p_k=sum_i a_i^k=Delta(a^k), 1≤k≤d. Since a^k∈A, each p_k belongs to the enveloping image. Thus a^⊗d belongs to that image, proving the first equality without a density, distribution or graded-Schur black box. The same argument shows that an operator commutes with U(g^e) iff it commutes with the diagonal tensor action of the invertible elements G_e=A^×; the reverse direction follows by differentiating (1+t a)^⊗d, and the forward direction by Newton identities.

If e has at least d distinct strings of length l, take the tensor of their top vectors. The l^d d! vectors obtained by individual powers 0≤r_i<l and all place permutations are distinct members of the Jordan tensor basis (string labels recover the permutation, and positions recover the powers). They give a copy of the regular right B-module, so the right action is injective. For d=0 both identities and injectivity are scalar identities. This stable argument is not used as a replacement for the full converse below.
 The preceding two local suppliers prove the full normal orbit closure, codimension-two extension and polynomial covariance. Evaluate the latter at e, discard powers≥l and obtain the second equality with the correct opposite right-action convention. Every claimed geometric and invariant-theoretic input is explicitly proved in those suppliers.

items.title: The shifted Yangian and the pyramid generators of the type-A finite W-algebra
items.statement: The shifted Yangian Y_n(σ) has the shifted Drinfeld D,E,F relations and higher root generators, with s_ij=p_j−p_i for i≤j and0 otherwise. Its canonical filtration gives the rth modes degree r, and its loop filtration gives them degree r−1; these filtrations have different associated graded algebras. W(λ) is its quotient by D_1^(r), r>p_1. It has a PBW set of Gauss generators with s_ij<r≤s_ij+p_min(i,j), including 1≤r≤p_i on the diagonal. Higher D_i modes are polynomial expressions and are not all zero. Define T(u)=F(u)D(u)E(u), with T_ij(u)=sum_(r≥0) T_ij^(r) u^−r and T_ij^(0)=delta_ij, with no additional u^s_ij multiplier. Its modes vanish for 0<r≤s_ij. In the finite quotient they also vanish for r>S_ij=s_ij+p_min(i,j), so the finite PBW indices are exactly s_ij<r≤S_ij. The auxiliary signed path polynomials used to construct these Gauss generators must not all be identified with these shifted T modes. Root weights are ε_i−ε_j; the surviving modes have loop leading term (−1)^(r−1)e_ij;r−1.

items.title: Gan-Ginzburg and Skryabin inputs for the type-A pyramid good grading
items.statement:
Keep the pyramid data $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$
of [[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]] and
the finite W-algebra $W(\lambda)$, the bimodule $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$
and the Whittaker category of
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Double the pyramid
grading by declaring the degree of $e_{i,j}$ to be
$2(\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i))$; then $e$ has degree $2$ and the
degree $-1$ part of $\mathfrak g$ is zero. Let
$\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r>0,\ r\ \mathrm{even}}\mathfrak g_{-r}$ in the doubled
grading (the strictly negative even part), carrying the character $\chi$. Then:

1. There is a homogeneous transverse complement
   $S=e+\ker(\operatorname{ad} f)$ for a suitable $f\in\mathfrak g$, and the
   conjugation map $M_{\mathrm{unip}}\times S\to e+\mathfrak m^\perp$,
   $(u,s)\mapsto usu^{-1}$, is a polynomial isomorphism; the Kazhdan
   associated graded of $Q_\chi$ is $\mathbb C[M_{\mathrm{unip}}]\otimes\mathbb C[S]$
   and $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)=\mathbb C[S]$.
2. Assuming the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], for every $W(\lambda)$-module $X$, the twisted $\mathfrak m$-cohomology of
   $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}X$ vanishes in positive degree and its degree-zero
   part is $X$.
3. Every nonzero module on which all $x-\chi(x)$, $x\in\mathfrak m$, act
   locally nilpotently has a nonzero simultaneous invariant vector; in
   particular $\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M$ in the Whittaker
   category.

These assertions use the doubled good grading; no nondegenerate alternating
form on the original degree $-1$ space is asserted.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The pyramid data, the doubled grading $\deg e_{i,j}=2(\mathrm{col}(j)-\mathrm{col}(i))$, the subspaces $\mathfrak m,\mathfrak p$ in the doubled grading, the ideals $I_\chi$, $U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ and the bimodule $Q_\chi$, and the finite W-algebra $W(\lambda)$. For assertion (2), assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; assertions (1) and (3) do not require it.

[F1] In the doubled grading the only nonzero even degrees occur, $e$ has degree $2$, $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$ and $\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{r<0}\mathfrak g_r$ consist of even degrees only, and the string computation of the pyramid gives $\mathfrak m^\perp=[\mathfrak m,e]\oplus\ker(\operatorname{ad} f)$ for an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triple $(e,h,f)$ adapted to the grading ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], [[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]).

[F2] Chevalley-Eilenberg theory: the $\mathfrak m$-cohomology of a module is computed by the Chevalley-Eilenberg complex, $H^0$ is the space of invariants, and a short exact sequence of $\mathfrak m$-modules gives a long exact cohomology sequence ([[def-chevalley-eilenberg-cochains]], [[def-chevalley-eilenberg-differential]], [[def-lie-algebra-cohomology]], [[prop-zero-th-lie-algebra-cohomology-is-invariants]], [[thm-long-exact-sequence-in-lie-algebra-cohomology]]).

[F3] PBW orders the nonnegative-degree algebra $\mathfrak p$ before $\mathfrak m$ and replaces the rightmost $\mathfrak m$ generators by their character in $Q_\chi$. The resulting Kazhdan filtration is exhaustive, separated and bounded below; its symbols are polynomial functions on $e+\mathfrak m^\perp$. The twisted $\mathfrak m$ action has as symbol the infinitesimal conjugation action. These assertions follow by reordering the enveloping-algebra relations and the character quotient; no transverse Clifford factor is present in this even grading ([[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]], [[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]).


[F4] The Axiom of Choice permits the right-module splittings used in the bounded augmented complex for assertion (2) ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). No choice principle is invoked in assertions (1) and (3).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The doubled grading, the transverse slice $S$ and the bimodule $Q_\chi$; assume AC for assertion (2), as in [F4].

1.1 **Positive-weight transverse product.** Choose the usual rowwise $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ triple. On $\operatorname{Hom}(R_b,R_a)$ the strings have highest $h$-weight $p_a+p_b-2k$, $1\le k\le\min(p_a,p_b)$. Since the pyramid grading element differs from $h$ by row scalars, their highest and lowest grading weights are $2(p_b-k)\ge0$ and $-2(p_a-k)\le0$. Thus the negative-degree part is injected by $\operatorname{ad}e$ and gives the direct-sum complement of [F1]. The differential of $\alpha(u,z)=uzu^{-1}$ at $(1,e)$ is $(x,y)\mapsto[x,e]+y$, an isomorphism. Use weight $-H$ on $\mathfrak m$ and weight $2-H$ on the translated slice and target coordinates; these are positive. In homogeneous coordinates of increasing weight, each component of $\alpha$ is an invertible linear block in the variables of that weight plus a polynomial in lower-weight variables. Successive substitution constructs its polynomial inverse. In particular derivative invertibility alone is not being used as a global inverse theorem. [F1, F3, construct, algebra]

1.2 **Detection.** The shifted operators $x-\chi(x)$ form a representation of the nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak m$, because $\chi$ kills brackets. A nonzero central element has a nonzero kernel on any nonzero locally nilpotent module: apply its largest nonvanishing power to a nonzero vector. That kernel is stable, and the quotient Lie algebra acts on it with the same local nilpotence. Induction on $\dim\mathfrak m$ therefore gives a common nonzero invariant. The case $\mathfrak m=0$ is immediate. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 **The actual graded complex.** PBW and [F3] give $\operatorname{gr}Q_\chi=\mathbb C[e+\mathfrak m^\perp]$, with no additional symbol factor. Step 1.1 identifies this with $\mathbb C[M_{\mathrm{unip}}]\otimes\mathbb C[S]$. Infinitesimal conjugation acts by invariant vector fields on the first factor and trivially on the slice factor. Giving the exterior dual of a grading-degree $-2r$ vector weight $2r$ makes the twisted Chevalley–Eilenberg differential filtration preserving. Its graded complex is the polynomial de Rham complex of $M_{\mathrm{unip}}$, tensored with $\mathbb C[S]$: invariant vector fields trivialize the tangent bundle and the bracket terms are precisely the de Rham differential. Polynomial exponential coordinates identify this unipotent group with affine space. On a polynomial form of positive total degree $t$, $t^{-1}\iota_{\mathrm{Euler}}$ is a contracting homotopy; constants are the only surviving degree-zero classes. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 **Filtered lifting and right freeness.** A positive-degree cocycle in the actual complex has a graded leading term which is a boundary by step 2.1. Lift that boundary and subtract it, strictly lowering the integer filtration degree; boundedness below terminates this process. The same procedure lifts every graded invariant, using vanishing of graded degree-one cohomology to remove its differential. Hence $H^{>0}(\mathfrak m,Q_\chi)=0$ and $\operatorname{gr}W=\mathbb C[S]$, since $H^0(\mathfrak m,Q_\chi)=W$ by the defining invariant realization. Using the fixed PBW vector-space identification $U(\mathfrak p)\to Q_\chi$, take homogeneous coordinate representatives in $U(\mathfrak p)$ and form their ordered products there before projecting to $Q_\chi$. This never multiplies abstract classes in a left-ideal quotient. Their projected ordered monomials, acted on by the right $W$ bimodule action, span $Q_\chi$ by finite descending leading-term subtraction. A finite relation among them would give a relation between distinct monomials over $\operatorname{gr}W$; independence of polynomial monomials rules this out. Thus $Q_\chi$ is right $W$-free. All statements include the independent scalar coordinate of $\mathfrak{gl}_N$. [F2, F3, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 **Transfer to every module without graded-flatness assumptions.** The finite augmented cochain complex $0\to W\to C^0\to\cdots\to C^{\dim\mathfrak m}\to0$, where $C^j=Q_\chi\otimes\bigwedge^j\mathfrak m^*$, is exact by step 3.1 and is a complex of right $W$-modules. Its differentials are right $W$-linear because the right action commutes with the twisted left $\mathfrak m$ action. Each term is right $W$-free. Starting at the last term, split each surjection onto the already-projective boundary module; descending induction makes every boundary projective and splits every short exact sequence, including $W\hookrightarrow C^0$. These splittings supply a right $W$-linear contraction of the augmented complex. Tensor the contraction with an arbitrary left $W$-module $X$. This remains a contraction, and the resulting complex is exactly the twisted Chevalley–Eilenberg complex of $Q_\chi\otimes_W X$. Consequently its positive cohomology vanishes and its degree-zero cohomology is $X$ via $x\mapsto1_\chi\otimes x$. No filtration or flatness of $X$ is assumed. The splittings use exactly [F4]. [F2, F4, step 3.1, choose, construct, algebra]

5.1 The preceding steps prove the three assertions with the doubled even grading. In particular there is no degree $-1$ symplectic or Clifford contribution. If $e=0$, then $\mathfrak m=0$ and the product, augmentation and all cohomology identities reduce to their degree-zero identities. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- The role of the doubling is to put the contracting $\mathbb C^\times$-weights in even degrees so that the Kazhdan symbols are the coordinate functions of the unipotent group; the loop filtration of the finite W-algebra is a different filtration and is treated separately later on this page.

- The detection statement is the categorical form of Skryabin's theorem used to identify Whittaker vectors: for $M$ in the Whittaker category, $M\mapsto\mathrm{Wh}(M)$ loses nothing.

items.title: Ordered monomial PBW basis for the shifted Yangian
items.statement: For any fixed order on the shifted D,E,F root modes, their ordered monomials form a basis of Y_n(σ). Its canonical associated graded is the polynomial algebra on all those symbols; its loop associated graded is U(gl_n[t](σ)). In W(λ) the ordered monomials in the finite Gauss ranges s_ij<r≤s_ij+p_min(i,j) form a basis. Its commutative Kazhdan/canonical associated graded and its noncommutative loop associated graded are distinct. Equivalently the finite T coefficients with s_ij<r≤S_ij form an ordered PBW basis; r is the unshifted FDE coefficient index, not r−s_ij.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Straighten the finite parabolic relations by mode and root height. Prove unshifted independence using products of arbitrary evaluation matrices at finitely many distinct scalar points: the linearization of the first k current modes is a Vandermonde matrix, so every finite relation is detected at a sufficiently large finite jet. Apply finite-dimensional PBW to those jet Lie algebras; no finite-dimensional PBW theorem is silently applied directly to gl_n[t]. Shifted modes are the corresponding triangular subset. For W, straighten the D_1 truncation as in the preceding definition. At distinct scalar column matrices h_c I, the derivative of an allowed off-diagonal Gauss coefficient is z product_extra(1+h z)/(1+h_c z) for E, and z/(1+h_c z) for F. The first common-column coefficients are Vandermonde with nonzero extra-column factors; the diagonal elementary-coefficient Jacobian is Vandermonde as well. Hence the finite symbols are independent. Their degrees match the doubled-good-grading slice coordinates, whose polynomial PBW was proved by the GG supplier; equality of graded Hilbert series makes them generators. These explicit arguments are the affine-Yangian §3 and finite-W matrix §2 local proofs. The FDE coefficient change is triangular in the original index r. Lower modes0<r≤s_ij vanish; the column recursion gives upper vanishing r>S_ij. Hence the surviving T symbols have exactly the same finite Gauss coordinate count and loop labels (i,j,r−1)∈K.

items.title: Skryabin's equivalence for the type-A Whittaker pair
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], inherited from assertion (2) of the good-grading cohomology supplier.

Let $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$, $W(\lambda)$,
$Q_\chi$ and $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ be as in
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Then the functor
$$Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$$
is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor
$\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor
$?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the
exact functor
$$M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}\bigl((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X\bigr)$$
on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a
$W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map
$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$
is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms
$(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible,
and for the one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting
isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$
is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The pyramid data, the bimodule $Q_\chi$ and the Whittaker category of [[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]], and a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$. Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the arbitrary-module equivalence and transported tensor assertions.

[F1] For every $W(\lambda)$-module $M$, the twisted $\mathfrak m$-cohomology of $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M$ vanishes in positive degrees and its degree-zero part is $M$; for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$ the invariants detect vanishing ([[lem-gan-ginzburg-skryabin-inputs-hold-for-the-type-a-pyramid-good-grading]]).

[F2] $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ is a $(U(\mathfrak g),W(\lambda))$-bimodule, and tensoring the canonical element $1_\chi$ with a $W(\lambda)$-module gives a left adjoint to $\mathrm{Wh}$; the unit and counit are the natural maps $M\to\mathrm{Wh}(Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)$, $v\mapsto1_\chi\otimes v$ and $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}\mathrm{Wh}(M)\to M$, $u1_\chi\otimes v\mapsto uv$ ([[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]], [[def-universal-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F3] Chevalley-Eilenberg exactness: tensoring with a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module preserves the Whittaker category and is exact, and the long exact cohomology sequence computes the cohomology of extensions ([[def-chevalley-eilenberg-cochains]], [[thm-long-exact-sequence-in-lie-algebra-cohomology]]).

[F4] The loop-symbol computation: in PBW degree the leading system of the $\chi$-equations for the tensor identification is polynomial Taylor translation on $\mathbb C[M_{\mathrm{unip}}]$ with invertible constant term; the finite matrices $X,Y$ constructed from the prefix-$T$ formulas are inverse by degree recursion, and the coefficient index is the actual displacement $\mathrm{col}(a)-\mathrm{col}(b)$ with no $u^s$ reindexing ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], [[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The bimodule $Q_\chi$, a $W(\lambda)$-module $M$, a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, and the maps $\mu_{M,X}$; assume AC as specified above.

1.1 Unit and counit. The adjunction between $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-$ and $\mathrm{Wh}$ has the unit $u_M\colon M\to\mathrm{Wh}(Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)$ and counit $c_M\colon Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}\mathrm{Wh}(M)\to M$ of [F2]. For every $M$, the kernel and cokernel of $u_M$ and $c_M$ lie in the kernel of the invariants functor: applying $H^0$ to the unit and using the vanishing of [F1] identifies the composite with the identity; a short exact sequence argument with the long exact sequence of [F3] then shows that if $H^0$ of a map in the category is an isomorphism then the map is an isomorphism, since the kernel and cokernel have vanishing invariants and a nonzero object of the category has nonzero invariants by [F1]. Hence $u_M,c_M$ are isomorphisms and the two functors are quasi-inverse. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 Exactness and detection. Exactness of $\mathrm{Wh}$ follows because it is inverse to the exact functor $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-$ (tensoring with the right flat module $Q_\chi$, whose flatness is part of the free right-module structure of the source), and the detection statement is the case $H^0=0$ of [F1]. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 The transported tensor functor. For $M\in W(\lambda)$-mod and finite-dimensional $X$, the functor $M\mapsto\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X)$ is exact in $M$ because the composed functors are exact; it is the transport of $?\otimes X$ across the equivalence. [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Triangularity of the displayed tensor map.** Keep the polynomial-coordinate/distribution pairing from the good-grading calculation: the right-free PBW coordinates identify $Q_\chi\otimes_W M$ with the locally nilpotent coinduced model, by finite weighted Taylor pairing and descending leading-term subtraction, followed by filtered unions. Cofree evaluation on Whittaker vectors of this model tensored with $X$ gives a vector-space isomorphism $\ell:M\otimes X\to\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_W M)\otimes X)$. It is not the inverse of the displayed $\mu_{M,X}$ in general. Choose a common Engel flag $0=X_0\subset X_1\subset\cdots\subset X_t=X$ for the nilpotent $\mathfrak m$ action, so $\mathfrak m X_j\subset X_{j-1}$; a negative-graded Lie algebra acts nilpotently on a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module. The matrix-coefficient construction of $\ell$ preserves this flag and has diagonal $1_\chi\otimes m\otimes x_j$: on each flag quotient the $\mathfrak m$ action is trivial, and the inverse cofree evaluation is precisely the unit $m\mapsto1_\chi\otimes m$. Every correction term involves a strictly flag-lowering matrix coefficient. PBW represents these finitely supported lifts by elements of $U(\mathfrak p)$ acting on $M$; no completion of $M$ is used. The displayed map applies $\eta^{-1}$ of this representative to $M$ and leaves the $X$ component in its flag position. Thus $A=\mu_{M,X}\ell$ preserves $M\otimes X_j$ and is the identity on its successive quotients. Write $A=1+N$; then $N^t=0$, although its off-diagonal entries can be arbitrary operators on $M$. Hence $A^{-1}=\sum_{r=0}^{t-1}(-N)^r$, and $\mu_{M,X}$ is a vector-space isomorphism. This argument distinguishes cofree constant evaluation from the extension-dependent displayed map. [F1, F4, step 1.3, construct, algebra]

2.2 Associativity. The associativity isomorphisms of the transported functor are obtained by inserting the canonical associativity isomorphisms of the tensor product of $\mathfrak g$-modules into the definition of $\circledast$ and applying the inverse equivalence; they are compatible by the naturality of the unit and counit of the adjunction and by the coherence of the tensor associativity in $\mathcal C(\lambda)$. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 **Balancing and $W$-linearity.** PBW gives unique representatives $\eta(u)1_\chi$, $u\in U(\mathfrak p)$, in $Q_\chi$. Define $\psi_M(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)=um$. Since the right action of $w\in W\subset U(\mathfrak p)$ sends this representative to $\eta(uw)1_\chi$, the formula is right-$W$-balanced: $(uw)m=u(wm)$. Moreover $\psi_M(\eta(v)q\otimes m)=v\psi_M(q\otimes m)$ for $v\in U(\mathfrak p)$. The shift $\eta$ adds a Lie character on $\mathfrak p$, so on its primitive generators, and hence multiplicatively on $U(\mathfrak p)$, $(\eta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(v)=\Delta\eta(v)$. The $W$ action on the source Whittaker subspace is therefore $\Delta\eta(w)$, while the target restricted $\mathfrak p$-module $M\otimes X$ has action $\Delta(w)$. Applying $\psi_M\otimes\mathrm{id}$ to the displayed coproduct identity proves $\mu_{M,X}(wz)=w\mu_{M,X}(z)$. Together with step 2.1 this proves the actual stated $W$-module isomorphism. No equality with cofree evaluation or citation-only character-equation argument is used. [F2, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Independence of the order. For $X=V^{\otimes d}$ the isomorphism $\mu_d$ is the composite of the single-step maps $\mu_{\bullet,V}$; two different parenthesizations differ by the associativity isomorphisms of step 2.2, and both are restrictions of the balanced evaluation maps of step 3.1, applied with the same iterated coproduct on $U(\mathfrak p)$; coassociativity and the displayed shift identity make these maps equal. Therefore the resulting isomorphism $\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$ is independent of the composed associativity isomorphisms. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The source's convention is that $T_{i,j}^{(r)}$ carries the actual displacement index $r=\mathrm{col}(a)-\mathrm{col}(b)$; coefficients at or below the prefix shift vanish and coefficient $0$ is $\delta_{i,j}$. This is the convention used by the explicit matrices in step 2.1.

- The equivalence is exact but its left adjoint in the Schur-functor constructions later on this page is not the naive tensor functor; those constructions use the projective generator $T$ of a single block, treated later.

items.title: The loop filtration on the type-A finite W-algebra has associated graded U(g^e)
items.statement: Equip $W(\lambda)$ with the loop (good) filtration $F_rW(\lambda)=W(\lambda)\cap\bigoplus_{s\le r}U(\mathfrak p)_s$ induced by the pyramid grading $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$. Then the associated graded algebra $\mathrm{gr}\,W(\lambda)$ is canonically isomorphic to the enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, viewed as a graded algebra via the restriction of the pyramid grading to the centralizer $\mathfrak g^e$, and the isomorphism sends the leading symbol of the generator $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ to $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$ (with the elements $e_{i,j;r}$ the basis of $\mathfrak g^e$ of the previous items). In particular $W(\lambda)$ is a filtered deformation of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and the loop filtration is separated: the ordered monomials in the generators $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$, form a basis of $W(\lambda)$. This filtration is not the Kazhdan filtration: the Kazhdan filtration has associated graded $\mathbb C[S]$ (a commutative Slodowy slice algebra), while here $\mathrm{gr}\,W(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g^e)$ is noncommutative in general. Neither the loop filtration nor its associated graded requires the Kazhdan grading of the Gan-Ginzburg quantization.
items.strategy: Use the shifted-Yangian presentation: $W(\lambda)$ is generated by the $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ and its ordered monomials form a basis by the PBW theorem of the previous items; compute the leading symbols in the associated graded of $U(\mathfrak p)$ using [BKHL, Lemma 3.1] and [BK3, Lemma 3.4], which give $\mathrm{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)}=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$. Since the $e_{i,j;r}$ form a basis of $\mathfrak g^e$ and satisfy the same PBW relations, comparing ordered monomials with the PBW basis of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ gives the algebra isomorphism. This is the proof of [BKHL, Lemma 3.1]; the same statement is [BGK, Theorem 3.8] for arbitrary good gradings, proved via the Kazhdan-filtration comparison with the Gan-Ginzburg quantization. Record explicitly that the filtration here is the good (loop) filtration: [BGK, Section 3.3] distinguishes it from the Kazhdan filtration, and only the former is used by the double centralizer argument. Use exactly the supplier-defined K: T_ij^(r+1), s_ij≤r<p_j, has loop degree r and leading symbol (−1)^r e_ij;r. Equivalently its coefficient index k=r+1 satisfies s_ij<k≤S_ij=p_j in the left-justified convention. T=FDE has no scalar u-shift. Its coefficient PBW basis and the bijection J↔K match the same centralizer PBW basis.

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra
items.statement:
Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The degenerate affine Hecke algebra $H_d$, a multiset $\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_l)$ of arbitrary complex numbers with $l\ge1$, and its quotient $A=H_d/(f(x_1))$, where $f(t)=\prod_j(t-a_j)$ and the ideal is two-sided. Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the Skryabin/tensor realization used in PBW independence.

[F1] The affine ordered monomials form a basis, $x_i$ commute, and the cross relations are $s_ix_{i+1}=x_is_i+1$ and $s_ix_i=x_{i+1}s_i-1$. Its generator-fixing anti-involution exists ([[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]).

[F2] The pyramid construction provides $\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak m,e,\chi$ and the automorphism $\eta(E_{ab})=E_{ab}+\delta_{ab}(n-\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h)$. The Whittaker bimodule is $Q_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)I_\chi$ with right $W$-action by $\eta$. PBW identifies it as a vector space with $U(\mathfrak p)$ ([[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], [[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]], [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]).

[F3] For any $\mathfrak p$-module $M$ and finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the tensor-isomorphism of [[thm-skryabins-equivalence-for-the-type-a-whittaker-pair]] identifies $\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_W M)\otimes X)$ with $M\otimes X$ by $(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes v\mapsto um\otimes v$. These identifications are natural and compatible with tensor associativity. No cyclotomic quotient is part of this input.

[F4] The Casimir operators on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ satisfy the affine Hecke relations, commute with $\mathfrak g$, and therefore restrict to Whittaker vectors; their naturality transports them through F3 ([[thm-the-casimir-and-place-permutation-operators-satisfy-degenerate-affine-hecke-relations]]).

[F5] Filtered leading symbols multiply in the associated graded ([[def-associated-graded-algebra-of-a-filtered-algebra]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** $A=H_d/(f(x_1))$, the polynomial-degree filtration, and F1–F5; assume AC for F3 and the transported representation.

1.1 Bounded spanning in every variable. For each $r$, put $w_r=s_{r-1}\cdots s_1$ (and $w_1=1$). In the affine algebra the cross relations give $w_rx_1w_r^{-1}=x_r+$ terms of polynomial degree zero. Hence $w_rf(x_1)w_r^{-1}=x_r^l+$ terms of degree at most $l-1$. This element is zero in $A$. Every affine ordered monomial with an exponent at least $l$ can therefore have a factor $x_r^l$ replaced by terms of strictly smaller total polynomial degree; straightening those terms never increases that degree. Induction on total degree, applied to every such replacement, expresses every monomial as a linear combination of $x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$ with $0\le r_i<l$. The same induction proves that $F_mA$ is spanned by bounded monomials of degree at most $m$. [F1, algebra]

1.2 A realization for arbitrary complex roots. For $d\ge1$ choose an integer $n\ge d$ and the rectangular partition $\lambda=(l,\ldots,l)$ with $n$ rows, so every column has height $q_j=n$ and $e$ has $n$ strings of length $l$. On $\mathfrak p$ define the one-dimensional module $\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}$ by $E_{ab}\mapsto\delta_{ab}a_{\mathrm{col}(a)}$. This is a Lie character: it vanishes on the strictly positive nilradical and is $a_j$ times the trace on the $j$th Levi block. In particular no integrality or coset condition on $a_j$ is needed. Restrict this module to $W$ and use F3 with $X=V^{\otimes d}$. Restrict the affine Hecke operators on $(Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_{\mathbf a})\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ to Whittaker vectors, then transport through F3. This defines an affine Hecke action on $V_{\mathbf a}^{\otimes d}=\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}\otimes V^{\otimes d}$; the $s_i$ are place permutations. The following step computes $x_1$ before asserting any quotient factorization. [F2, F3, F4, construct]

1.3 The transported first operator. Write $Q_c=Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}$ and define $\pi_c:Q_c\to\mathbb C$ by $\pi_c(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes1)=u\cdot1$. It is well defined: the right $W$-relations become multiplication by the restricted character, and PBW gives representatives $\eta(u)1_\chi$. For a tensor basis vector $v_{\mathbf j}$ write its unique Whittaker preimage under F3 as $z=\sum_{\mathbf i}z_{\mathbf i}\otimes v_{\mathbf i}$, with $z_{\mathbf i}\in Q_c$. Then $\pi_c(z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$. If $\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b)$, then $E_{ab}\in\mathfrak p$ and $\pi_c(E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{ab}(a_{\mathrm{col}(a)}+\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h-n)\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$, since $\eta^{-1}(E_{ab})=E_{ab}-\delta_{ab}(n-\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h)$. If $\mathrm{col}(a)>\mathrm{col}(b)$, the Whittaker equation for $E_{ab}$ instead gives $E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i}=\chi(E_{ab})z_{\mathbf i}-\sum_{\mathbf k}z_{\mathbf k}$, where $\mathbf k$ runs over tensors obtained from $\mathbf i$ by replacing an occurrence of $a$ by $b$. Apply $\pi_c\otimes1$ to $\Omega_{01}z=\sum_{a,b,\mathbf i}E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i}\otimes E_{ba}^{(1)}v_{\mathbf i}$. The terms with $\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b)$ give $(a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}+\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(j_1)}q_h-n)v_{\mathbf j}$. The $\chi$ term gives $v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}$, because $\chi(E_{ab})=1$ exactly when $b=L(a)$. In the negative sum, replacing the first occurrence gives $-\sum_{h>\mathrm{col}(j_1)}q_h\,v_{\mathbf j}$; replacing an occurrence in position $k>1$ gives $-v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}$ exactly when $\mathrm{col}(j_k)<\mathrm{col}(j_1)$. Consequently the transported right action is
$$v_{\mathbf j}x_1=v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}+(a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}+q_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}-n)v_{\mathbf j}-\sum_{k>1:\ \mathrm{col}(j_k)<\mathrm{col}(j_1)}v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}.$$
Here a nonexistent left-shift term is zero. In our rectangle $q_j=n$, so the diagonal coefficient is precisely $a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 The cyclotomic relation and the leading symbols. Let $C_k$ be the span of tensors whose first entry has column at most $k$, with $C_0=0$. Step 1.3 gives $C_k(x_1-a_k)\subseteq C_{k-1}$: both the left shift and every exchange strictly lower the first column, while $x_1$ preserves $C_{k-1}$. Thus successively applying $(x_1-a_l),\ldots,(x_1-a_1)$ kills $C_l=V^{\otimes d}$. The factors commute, so $f(x_1)=0$ and the action factors through $A$. Grade $V$ by $\deg v_b=l-\mathrm{col}(b)$ and give its endomorphism algebra the induced filtration. In step 1.3 the left shift has degree one and every other term has total tensor degree zero. Hence $\operatorname{gr}_1x_1=e_1$. The recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ shows by induction that all $x_j$ are filtered of degree one with leading symbol $e_j$, and that $s_j$ have degree zero with symbols the place permutations. [F1, F5, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Independence and the associated graded algebra. The cross relations and the conjugated relations in step 1.1 give a surjection $B=\mathbb C[X_1,\ldots,X_d]/(X_1^l,\ldots,X_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}A$. Its composite with the associated graded tensor representation is $X_j\mapsto e_j$, $w\mapsto$ place permutation. Choose the rightmost box in each of $d$ distinct rows and let $v$ be the tensor of those boxes. For bounded $\mathbf r$ and $w$, the vectors $v e_1^{r_1}\cdots e_d^{r_d}w$ are distinct tensor basis vectors: their row labels identify the permutation, and their columns identify all $r_i$. Therefore this composite is injective. It follows that $B\cong\operatorname{gr}A$. Taking leading symbols of a hypothetical linear relation among bounded monomials, first in its largest total degree and then inductively, proves their independence. Along with step 1.1 this gives the claimed PBW basis, its filtration compatibility, and $\dim A=l^dd!$. The longest strings have length $l$, the number of columns, and there are $n=q_l\ge d$ of them; no column height is used as their length. For $d=0$ the algebra, basis and associated graded are all $\mathbb C$, so the assertions hold directly. [F1, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Integral roots and the pyramid dictionary. For integral roots write $m_i=\#\{j:a_j=i\}$; then $f(x_1)=\prod_i(x_1-i)^{m_i}$, the quotient attached to $\Lambda=\sum_i m_i\Lambda_i$. For arbitrary complex roots the same algebraic definition applies, with integer-chain bookkeeping separately in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$. The rectangle above has $c_j=a_j$ and $q_j=n$, hence $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$; the general pyramid dictionary is the displayed diagonal term of step 1.3. No general complex root is identified with an integer-only fundamental-weight index. [step 1.3, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 Level one and the anti-involution. For $l=1$, $x_1=a_1$ and $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ give $x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ by induction; the basis of step 3.1 identifies the quotient with $\mathbb C[S_d]$. The generator-fixing anti-involution fixes $f(x_1)$ and preserves its two-sided ideal, so descends to $A$. [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

4.3 The graded top pairing. Put $D=d(l-1)$ and $T=x_1^{l-1}\cdots x_d^{l-1}$. Let $\tau_0:B\to\mathbb C$ be the coefficient of $X_1^{l-1}\cdots X_d^{l-1}\cdot1$. For graded monomials $X^{\mathbf r}w,X^{\mathbf s}v$, this coefficient is one exactly when $wv=1$ and $\mathbf r+w(\mathbf s)=(l-1,\ldots,l-1)$, and is zero otherwise. The equivalent reversed condition is $vw=1$ and $\mathbf s+w^{-1}(\mathbf r)=(l-1,\ldots,l-1)$; thus $\tau_0$ is symmetric. Each basis element pairs with its unique complementary element, so the pairing is perfect, including between degrees $m$ and $D-m$. Define $\tau:A\to\mathbb C$ as the coefficient of $T\cdot1$ in the PBW basis. By filtration compatibility $\tau=\tau_0\circ\operatorname{gr}_D$ on $A=F_DA$, and it vanishes on $F_{D-1}A$. Therefore, if $a\in F_mA$ and $b\in F_{D-m}A$, then $\tau(ab)=\tau_0(\operatorname{gr}_m(a)\operatorname{gr}_{D-m}(b))=\tau(ba)$. This establishes cyclicity only under the stated degree bound so far. [F5, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Full generator cyclicity. Since permutations have degree zero, step 4.3 gives $\tau(aw)=\tau(wa)$ for every $a\in A$, $w\in S_d$. To check $\tau(x_i b)=\tau(bx_i)$ for all bounded basis monomials $b$, step 4.3 suffices when $\deg b<D$. The remaining ones are exactly $b=Tw$. The polynomial $T$ is central: it commutes with the $x_j$, and the cross relations directly give $s_j(x_jx_{j+1})=(x_jx_{j+1})s_j$, while $s_j$ commutes with the other variables. Hence $s_jT=Ts_j$. Applying the already proved permutation cyclicity twice gives $\tau(x_iTw)=\tau(wx_iT)=\tau(wTx_i)=\tau(Twx_i)$. This proves cyclicity with every generator on every element; successively moving generators of a word from the beginning to the end proves $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ for all $a,b\in A$. It also covers $l=1$ (where $T=1$ and $D=0$). [F1, step 4.3, algebra]

6.1 Nondegeneracy and block restriction. For $0\ne a\in A$, take its largest filtration degree $m$, so $\operatorname{gr}_m(a)\ne0$. By the perfect graded pairing of step 4.3 choose homogeneous $b_0\in B_{D-m}$ with $\tau_0(\operatorname{gr}_m(a)b_0)\ne0$, and lift it to $b\in F_{D-m}A$. Then $\tau(ab)\ne0$. Thus the pairing has zero left radical, and symmetry gives zero right radical; this proves nondegeneracy without claiming that products of excess total degree have zero trace. If $e$ is a central idempotent and $0\ne a\in eA$, choose $b$ as above; then $\tau(aeb)=\tau(ab)\ne0$, so the restriction to $eA=eAe$ is nondegenerate and symmetric as well. [F5, step 4.3, step 5.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The integer and nonintegral cases are kept separate on purpose: the integral case is the classical cyclotomic quotient of the type-A root system, while the general complex roots are handled through the pyramid realization whose columns are chosen large enough to make the tensor action faithful.

- The trace of steps 4.3, 5.1 and 6.1 is the top PBW coefficient functional; it is the tool that rules out nonzero ideals in the radical in the double centralizer arguments on this page.

items.title: The parabolic highest-weight truncation factors through the cyclotomic quotient
items.statement: For a nonempty pyramid and arbitrary complex origins c, put a_j=c_j+q_j−n. For d≥1, the raw tensor operator x_1 on V_c^tensor d has minimal polynomial exactly product_j(x−a_j), including repeated roots with their multiplicities. Thus its H_d action factors through H_d(a). The ordinary Casimir action on P_c tensor V^tensor d likewise factors through this polynomial when P_c is the ground induced module with its genuine column filtration. This does not assert that every unrelated standard N(A) or every parabolic category-O object carries that same tensor action. For d=0 there is no x_1. Integral-root Λ and arbitrary-root coset Λ use the separate conventions in the preceding definition.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. The first tensor step of P_c has a column filtration; its scalar on the jth quotient is a_j by the trace Casimir difference. Successively apply x_1−a_j along that filtration to annihilate the tensor module; tensoring the remaining factors retains this identity. Transfer it through the explicit Skryabin tensor matrix to the raw space. Assign v_i column degree col(i); the leading x_1 is e on the first factor, whose largest string has length l. A polynomial of degree<l would have a nonzero leading e power and cannot vanish. Thus the degree-l polynomial is minimal, also when roots coincide. This proof needs no integral category-O identification for arbitrary c and no blanket assertion about all x_j eigenvalues.

items.title: The deformed tensor space for the type-A finite W-algebra
items.statement:
Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.
items.strategy: Assume AC for the actual Skryabin and Vust suppliers. The column-trace Lie character $\kappa_c(X)=\sum_b c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb})$ defines the total origin twist once. Use the actual balanced $\mu$ and ambient trace-form Casimir; evaluation on its Whittaker preimages separates nonnegative-column terms, negative character terms, first-position replacements and cross-position replacements, giving exactly the displayed raw $x_1$. Thus affine relations and commutation are transported with $W$, not with all of $\mathfrak p$. First-column filtration gives the full cyclotomic polynomial, and the total tensor grading gives its exact minimal degree, including repeated roots. Restrict the column character to the fixed basis: $\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{ij}\delta_{r0}\sum_{b\le p_i}c_b$. The graded automorphism $\tau_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ preserves $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, and the full fixed-chart graded representation is $\operatorname{gr}\Phi_{d,c}=\varphi_{d,0}\tau_c\zeta$, including its surviving degree-zero scalar. Keep the actual $T=FDE$ coefficient index, $T^{(r+1)}$ loop degree $r$ and sign $(-1)^r$. The right symbols are individual $e$ operators and places. Since $\tau_c$ is a unital automorphism, the exact character-twisted representation has the same unital graded image and commutant as untwisted Vust. Prove the two full filtered centralizer identities by the chains $A^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)\subseteq Z(D^0)=A^0$ and its reverse counterpart, then finite descending subtraction. Handle $d=0$ with the nontrivial character on the scalar module and the empty pyramid by its zero/scalar identities. Rank-one $c_1=1,d=1$ yields fixed generator $E_{11}=2$, not untwisted $1$; the $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ example gives $[E_{11}-E_{22},x_1]=2E_{12}\ne0$. All origins, shapes and degrees are retained; no stable range or admissibility is used. Mathematical acceptance and actual-supplier/consumer closure remain with the original reviewer.
