items.title: The Whittaker functor from the relevant parabolic category-O summand
items.statement: On genuine parabolic O the Whittaker functor V is D_row Wh D_row, using restricted duality for the row-sum torus and the reflected head/tail identification; equivalently it is the appropriate continuous χ-coinvariant functor. It is exact on these U(m)-finitely-generated objects and intertwines finite tensoring, Casimir and flips. It is distinct from the subsequent Hecke quotient Hom_g(T,−). For admissible c define O_c^d from column-strict labels with nonnegative integral differences from each column's ground entries, P_c the ground simple projective-injective and T=P_c tensor V^tensor d. Then V(P_c)=C_c, V(T)=V_c^tensor d, and V(K(A)) is the simple W-module L(A) for Std labels and zero offStd. Nonintegral cosets have an explicit typed equivalence to products of the integral models; no arbitrary complex c is called an integral block of page16. The tensor compatibility is coherent and preserves x,s. After fixing the ground identification i_0:V(P_c)→C_c, the resulting compatible functor and j_d are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism. Without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Use lower-central weights on U(m) to make its augmentation Rees algebra an image of the enveloping algebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra generated by y_i t^r, 0≤r≤w_i. PBW/Hilbert gives noetherianity; Rees submodule finiteness gives Artin–Rees for left ideals. Baer's criterion then proves the continuous dual union(U/I^k)* injective. Evaluation at1 identifies Hom_m(M,Eχ) with χ-finite functionals; the right action is λu(v)=λ(uv), so its E-valued expression is λ(u r v). The row-sum torus has χ weight0; finite U(m) generation makes these Hom spaces finite, giving exactness after restricted duality. Skryabin supplies the reflected head/tail W action. For nonintegral origins use the actual all-weight page13 adjoint-finite Verma theorem: tensor-projective Hom matrices identify the fixed-character Harish–Chandra category with the ordinary O linkage block. Ore twists across adjacent different integer cosets are exact by injective lowering and flat localization; their Verma highest vector F^−1v has s-dot weight, and the finite nilpotent tensor expansion identifies their invariant Hom matrices. Stable coset sorting preserves final Levi simple roots, hence the parabolic Serre subcategories and their largest generalized-Verma quotients. Shift a in a coset to a−cκ+n−nκ; choose common lower alphabet large enough, giving page16 column heights exactly q_j. For standard characters the Levi Weyl numerator is det(z_r^a_s) times the common factor product z_r^(n−1); the offsets cancel exactly. Classical Cauchy from Schur–Weyl identifies these nested-row minors with the actual16 highest projection, so offStd simple characters vanish. Its kernel is stable under residue operators; irreducibility of the highest component and nonzero ground force every Std image nonzero. Apply the two filtered-centralizer lifting arguments locally, independent of the later collector. T has only Std socle, so V is faithful on End T; surjectivity of the raw Hecke image gives End_g(T)^op=B_d. Factor exact V through the corner quotient Hom_g(T,−); its factor M tensor_B− is exact and faithful, hence M_B is a progenerator by projective-cover Nakayama. W_d=End_B(M) gives Morita and proves the Std images simple. The ZA polynomial-induction construction gives two-term add(T) copresentations of every projective; normalized tensor compatibility determines the natural isomorphism on T, then on all projectives via these kernels, then on all objects via projective presentations. Determinant shifts embed each finite coset chunk in a polynomial chunk. The Whittaker, HC, coset-label, quotient and Specht-corner local notes expand every step; no BG, KSX or W-simple-classification black box is required.

items.title: The finite-W and degenerate cyclotomic Hecke actions satisfy the double centralizer property
items.statement: For every complex origin c and every d, the raw tensor image algebras W_d and B_d=H_d(λ,c) are mutual centralizers on V_c^tensor d. Their graded image algebras are the corresponding U(g^e) and truncated polynomial/permutation images. If q_l≥d the H_d(a) action is faithful. Morita equivalence via Hom_W(V_c^tensor d,−) additionally holds for admissible origins, meaning c_i−c_j∈Z implies c_i=c_j, as proved by the actual Whittaker quotient construction below. Mutual centralizers alone do not imply Morita for arbitrary c; the explicit c=(0,1), q=(1,1), d=2 example has a nonprojective tensor module.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. For each filtered centralizer, its leading symbol lies in the corresponding graded centralizer. Vust supplies an element of the opposite algebra with that symbol. Lift it by the actual W loop basis or cyclotomic bounded monomials, subtract and descend the finite tensor filtration. This proves both equalities and both graded-image assertions; it is a two-sided leading-symbol argument, not an unjustified inherited double commutant. The longest-string graded vector gives stable injectivity. Under admissibility, the independent Whittaker character/Serre-quotient proof makes the tensor module a right B_d progenerator, and the first identity then gives Morita. The exact nonadmissible finite matrix in Whittaker-quotient §8 separates these assertions.

items.title: The Whittaker functor is exact and fully faithful on the required projectives
items.statement: For admissible c the genuine Whittaker functor is exact on O_c^d, and γ:Hom_g(T,−)→Hom_W(V_c^tensor d,V(−)) is a natural isomorphism. Both V and the Hecke quotient are fully faithful on ALL projective objects; the quotient is also fully faithful on tiltings. T is a self-dual prinjective detecting object containing all Std-labelled projective-injective covers, not a generator of the entire O summand. V(T) is a projective generator of W_d-mod and V preserves projectivity on add(T). It need not send every O projective to a W_d-projective. Its composite with the Morita equivalence is the Serre quotient killing exactly offStd simples.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Construct Z_A from finite column symmetric powers, embed it into V^tensor d by symmetrization and PBW induce. Split the last column and append its ground label: maximal physical-prefix inequalities force every possible larger polynomial label to retain that same ground column. Positive-radical invariants of a simple are its top Levi simple, proved using the nondegenerate contravariant form. Adjunction gives a single head; exact top centre sections and Levi BGG give the projective-cover character, so the lifted cover is an isomorphism. Induct over columns, then tensor the remaining finite symmetric powers. Specht-to-permutation dominance gives every projective cover once among these Z_A summands. The quotient T/Z_A has a standard flag, hence Std socle by actual16; its injective hull is in add(T). Thus every projective has a two-term add(T) copresentation. For the corner right adjoint G=Hom_B(eA,−), the unit on T is injective, splits by injectivity, and its torsion complementary summand vanishes by adjunction. Left exact G applied to a copresentation gives unit isomorphisms on every projective, proving full faithfulness. Modules with Std head and targets with Std socle give the same Hom argument, proving tilting faithfulness. Morita and the counit factorization give γ. The rank-one dominant Verma maps to a nonprojective simple over C[x]/x², while add(T) maps to projectives. The complete argument is Whittaker-quotient §§4–6, not the false full-generator inference.

items.title: The higher-level Schur-Weyl projective generator and Schur functor
items.statement: For admissible origins, T_α is the central component of the self-dual prinjective detector T=P_c tensor V^tensor d. On the integral model it is sum_(i∈I_α) f_i_d…f_i_1 P_c. Put B_α=End_g(T_α)^op, the corresponding component of the Hecke IMAGE algebra. The exact Schur quotient is π_α=Hom_g(T_α,−); its left adjoint π*_α=T_α tensor_(B_α)− is right exact. It sends B_α-projectives to O-projectives, and π*_α π_α recovers add(T_α), including every Std-labelled prinjective. Neither exactness of π* nor recovery of every O projective is asserted: both fail in the two-equal-charge rank-one example. These components assemble as locally unital sums; all ambient labels, including those killed by π, remain in the O category. The opposite composition/right-action convention is fixed throughout.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Use the actual Whittaker/Hecke factorization and choose a full finite O projective generator with T as a summand. Its idempotent e identifies π with e(−), giving exactness and the Serre quotient directly. Tensor-Hom gives the left adjoint and its right exactness. Free B modules map to copies of T, and projective summands remain projective. The evaluation isomorphism on add(T) proves the recovery clause. In the rank-one block, π(P_dom)=C and π*π(P_dom)=T/xT is the costandard, not P_dom; tensoring (x)→B with the C summand of T_B shows failure of exactness. AC is inherited from projective covers, duality and the locally unital assembly. This is Whittaker-quotient §6.

items.title: Stable range and block idempotent corner for higher-level Schur-Weyl duality
items.statement: Stable range means at least d Jordan strings have maximum length l, equivalently q_l≥d. For every c this makes the raw H_d(a) action injective. For admissible c outside this range, its image is a central block sum f H_d(a) f; f is the sum of the central blocks supporting contractible simple labels after enlarging all columns to a stable pyramid and deleting the added ground rows. Generalized-eigenvalue sequence idempotents e(i) are not individually central; f is a sum of entire central blocks. Nonadmissible c still has its genuine image algebra and full tensor double centralizer, but the same central-corner/Morita conclusion is not inferred without admissibility.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. The longest-string vector proves stable injectivity on associated graded and hence the filtered algebra. To prove the central-corner clause, enlarge n and every q_j by r, preserving every root a_j; the added bottom entries are c_j+1−(n+k). Let e select degree0 on those rows. Ground minima plus fixed central content force all simple labels in a supporting block to be contractible, and highest-weight PBW shows e kills all other simple blocks. On a supported block, e of the enlarged tensor module is the original tensor module. The original graded first-centralizer argument identifies its W image with the e corner. Under the already-proved stable Morita equivalence this eM is a right progenerator exactly for the supporting central blocks, so its right annihilator is their complement and the image is fHf. Row support and cyclicity are proved by the expanded two-row/induction argument in Specht-corner §§3–4; do not assume e is itself central.

items.title: Hecke induction and restriction functors on degenerate cyclotomic blocks
items.statement: For H(a) and its root-coset block decomposition, restriction e_i selects the last generalized x_(d+1) eigenvalue i after the tower inclusion; induction f_i is the corresponding B_(d+1)u tensor_(B_d)−. The degree/central-component idempotent u is the actual last-eigenvalue projector, not a claim that its corner equals the source algebra. These functors are exact, biadjoint and commute with ordinary *-duality; their Grothendieck operators are adjoint for the projective/module Hom pairing. Integral roots use the integer type-A indexing; nonintegral roots use their separate integer-coset chains. The full H(a) tower is obtained in sufficiently large admissible stable realizations; the image towers use the compatible projected tensor actions.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. The first d Casimir operators on T_(d+1)=T_d tensor V are those on T_d tensor1, so every zero image operator remains zero and the image tower map is well defined. Tensor adjunction gives π_d(GN)=Res π_(d+1)(N). The offStd kernel is stable under residue tensor operators by the actual16 highest projection and positivity of simple coefficients, so exact biadjoints descend to the quotient. Uniqueness of adjoints identifies their induction with B_(d+1)u tensor_(B_d)− and proves exactness/biadjunction. Finite admissible stable realizations cover every requested full Hecke block. The top PBW symmetric trace and the contravariant form on T identify πD with ordinary *-duality via the balanced evaluation map; two-term copresentations and projective presentations extend the identity from T to every object. Thus the functors commute with duality and the pairing adjunction follows. No unsupported Koszul grading or arbitrary corner equality is used. See Whittaker-quotient §7.

items.title: Higher-level Schur-Weyl endomorphism isomorphism
items.statement: For admissible c, the right Hecke action gives End_g(P_c tensor V^tensor d)^op=B_d, the image H_d(λ,c). On each central component it gives End_g(T_α)^op=B_α=f_α H_α(a) f_α. Stable range gives B_d=H_d(a) and B_α=H_α(a); a single component is not identified with the entire degree-d algebra. Outside stable range the central-corner statement uses the preceding admissible-origin supplier. These are surjective endomorphism isomorphisms, with injectivity of the full action precisely as stated.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Wh is faithful on endomorphisms of T because any nonzero image has a Std socle. γ maps its Hom algebra into the raw W centralizer; the commuting right Hecke action already surjects onto that centralizer by the two-sided filtered lifting proof. Hence End_g(T)^op=B_d, respecting the right-action opposite. Project central idempotents to obtain the component equalities. Stable injectivity and the outside-range central support follow from the preceding definition. This does not use false preservation of all projectives under Wh.

items.statement: The raw W_d and Hecke image B_d are mutual centralizers for every complex origin. For admissible origins, V_c^tensor d is a Morita progenerator and Hom_W(V_c^tensor d,−) is the equivalence W_d-mod→B_d-mod. The genuine Whittaker functor followed by this equivalence is the exact Schur Serre quotient killing offStd simples. It is fully faithful on all O projectives and on tiltings. The left adjoint is right exact and recovers add(T), not automatically all projectives. Stable range replaces B_d by H_d(a); otherwise the admissible-origin central-corner component B_d=fH_d(a)f is used.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Collect the separately proved all-origin filtered centralizers, admissible-origin character/quotient Morita, exact γ, ZA two-term copresentation criterion, head/socle tilting criterion and precise adjoint. items.title: Schur functor images of standard, simple, projective and tilting objects
items.statement: For admissible origins, π(N(A)) is the intrinsic affine-induced Specht module S(A): its jth column contributes the Specht shape read from its nonnegative ground differences and evaluation at a_j=c_j+q_j−n, and the factors are induced along the affine Young subalgebra. π(K(A))=D(A) is simple for A∈Std and zero otherwise; Std labels give all distinct simples of the relevant Hecke image. For A∈Std, π(P(A)) is its projective cover Y(A) and π*π(P(A))=P(A). All ambient offStd projectives still have their genuine images, without a false projective-preservation assertion. Tilting images have the actual opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag coefficients, and π is fully faithful on tiltings. For B∈Std, [S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):K(B)]=d_(B,A)(1), using the actual typed singular/parabolic coefficient conventions; B offStd is not a simple Hecke label. All these interfaces are ungraded at parameter1.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. In a stable realization choose d distinct full ground rows; their regular graded Hecke vector gives the rank-one weight idempotent e_S and identifies Hom_W(M,−) with e_S(−). Its generators are row permutations and h(x_i)=e_S(−D_(n−d+i)^(2)+e2(c)+e1(c)+d−n−i+1)e_S. The canonical colour fibre of a finite Levi standard is the tensor product of the column Specht modules by ordinary Schur–Weyl; these corner x_i act as a_j plus their within-column Jucys sums. Row permutations generate the other colour fibres, and multinomial dimensions prove the intrinsic induced-Specht isomorphism. This replaces the false source equality with Hom_p, not a definition of S(A) by π. The cyclic highest-vector proof identifies W types and the stable enlargement/contractible corner extends the conclusion to the original pyramid. Exact quotient/Morita proves the simple claim; add(T) recovery and full-projective FF give the cover claim for Std. Apply exact π to the actual16 tilting standard flag and its typed multiplicity dictionary. Exactness gives the restricted-B comparison. Specht-corner §§1–4 contains the explicit corner/evaluation calculations.

items.title: The degenerate affine Hecke relations on two tensor factors
items.statement: For gl_2, M=V and d=2, let P_ab permute factors a,b of V^tensor3. Then x_1=P_01, s_1=P_12 and x_2=P_02+P_12. Their eight-by-eight tensor-basis matrices satisfy s_1²=1, [x_1,x_2]=0, s_1 x_2−x_1 s_1=1 and x_2 s_1−s_1 x_1=1. For v_1 tensor v_2 tensor v_1, x_1 s_1 sends it to v_1 tensor v_1 tensor v_2, while s_1 x_2 sends it to the sum of that vector and the original. The commutator [s_1,x_2] is not literally1; the affine cross relation has the distinct x_1 on its other side.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Write each P_ab as its permutation of the eight binary words. Products of the three transpositions verify both affine relations. Expand [P_01,P_02+P_12]; the two oriented three-cycles cancel. Enumerate the basis words to check the displayed example and all matrix entries; this finite example tests the normalization, not the general proof.

items.title: A Hecke action alone does not imply the double centralizer property
items.statement: Let $M=\mathbb C^2$ be the trivial $\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$-module, $V=\mathbb C^2$ the natural module and $d=1$. The Arakawa-Suzuki construction provides an action of $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$ on $M\otimes V\cong\mathbb C^4$ commuting with $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, but here $x_1=\Omega^{M,V}=0$, so the action is the evaluation action $x_1\mapsto0$ and $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(\mathbb C^4)=M_4(\mathbb C)$. On the other hand the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ in $\mathrm{End}(M\otimes V)$ is the subalgebra $1_{\mathbb C^2}\otimes M_2(\mathbb C)$, of dimension $4$. Hence the equality $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=\mathrm{End}_{H_d}(M\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ fails by a factor of $4$ in dimension, even though the Hecke action is genuine, commutes with $\mathfrak g$, and is natural in $M$. The other equality also fails: $\psi(H_1)=\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}\subsetneq\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak g}(M\otimes V)\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\otimes1$, of dimension $4$. The hypothesis that is missing is the truncated/deformed setup: the double centralizer theorem applies to the finite-W-algebra tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ over the pyramid (equivalently to $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ with the truncated polynomial algebra $C_l[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$), where the Hecke action is the cyclotomic quotient action and the algebra of the opposite side is the finite W-algebra, not $U(\mathfrak g)$.
items.strategy: Compute $x_1$ on $M\otimes V$: the Casimir tensor has its first tensor factor acting on the trivial module $M$, so $x_1=0$; this is a legitimate instance of the Arakawa-Suzuki action, since the construction assigns an $H_d$-action to every $\mathfrak g$-module $M$. Compute the two centralizers in the bases $\{u_a\otimes v_b\}$: $\mathrm{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)$ is all of $M_4$ because $H_1$ acts by scalars, while $\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=1\otimes M_2$ has dimension $4$; the other centralizer is $M_2\otimes1$ versus $\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}$. Hence both double centralizer equalities fail. This is not a counterexample to the higher-level Schur-Weyl theorem: it shows that the theorem needs the finite-W-algebra deformation/truncation hypotheses, and that a mere commuting Hecke action on an arbitrary tensor module is insufficient.

items.title: Vust's double centralizer in a small stable range
items.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$, so $n=2$, $l=1$, $q_1=2$, $N=2$, $e=0$, all boxes in one column and the grading is concentrated in degree $0$: $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g^e=\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $\mathfrak m=0$, $C_1[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1,\dots,x_d)=\mathbb C$, and $C_1[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]=\mathbb C[S_d]$. Verify Vust's double centralizer for $d=1,2$, which is the stable range for this $\lambda$ (at least $d$ parts equal to $l=1$ holds for $d\le2$). For $d=1$: $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V)=\mathbb C\cdot1=\psi_1(\mathbb C[S_1])$ and $\varphi_1(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))=\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V)$, as $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)\to\mathrm{End}(V)$ is surjective. For $d=2$: $V^{\otimes2}=S^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$, $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes2})=2=\dim\mathbb C[S_2]$ with $\psi_2$ injective, and $\dim\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb C[S_2]}(V^{\otimes2})=\dim\mathrm{End}(S^2V)+\dim\mathrm{End}(\Lambda^2V)=9+1=10=\dim\varphi_2(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))$; check the two decompositions explicitly (the flip acts as $+1$ on $S^2V$ and $-1$ on $\Lambda^2V$, and the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ is exactly the block-diagonal algebra of the two isotypic components).
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. One column has no left-neighbour boxes, so e=0, not E12. Then g^e=gl_2, m=0 and the truncated variables vanish. For d=1 matrix units span End V. For d=2 compute the symmetric and alternating tensor bases; the flip eigenvalues are ±1 and ordinary complete reducibility gives their full9+1 endomorphism blocks. Both irreducible constituents occur, so C[S_2] acts injectively. These checks realize the full Vust theorem in its actual stable range.

items.title: A block idempotent corner outside the stable range
items.statement: Take $\lambda=(1,1)$ (so $l=1$, two parts equal to $1$) and $d=3$: the stable range fails, because at least $3$ parts of $\lambda$ equal to $1$ is false. Here $H_3(\Lambda)=\mathbb C[S_3]$ (level $l=1$), of dimension $6$, while the image $H_3(\lambda,c)$ in $\mathrm{End}_\mathbb C(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}$, $V=\mathbb C^2$, has dimension $5$: for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$, $V^{\otimes3}=L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$, so $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ has dimension $1+4=5$, and it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Under the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ (trivial, sign and standard blocks), the map to $\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$ kills exactly the sign block; hence $H_3(\lambda,c)\cong f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ with $f$ the central idempotent of the trivial and standard blocks, and $f$ is the block idempotent corner of the Definition. Verify: $\dim f\mathbb C[S_3]f=1+4=5$, the map $\mathbb C[S_3]\twoheadrightarrow f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ is multiplication by $f$, and the antisymmetrizer $a=\sum_{w\in S_3}\mathrm{sgn}(w)w$ spans the kernel of the action on $V^{\otimes3}$ because $\Lambda^3V=0$ for $\dim V=2$.
items.strategy: Decompose $V^{\otimes3}$ for $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ by the classical Schur-Weyl rule: the partitions of $3$ with at most $2$ rows are $(3)$ and $(2,1)$, so $V^{\otimes3}\cong L(3)\oplus L(2,1)^{\oplus2}$; hence $\mathrm{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})\cong\mathbb C\times M_2$, of dimension $5$, and by Schur-Weyl duality it is the image of $\mathbb C[S_3]$. Compare with the Wedderburn decomposition $\mathbb C[S_3]\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2$: the sign block acts on $V^{\otimes3}$ by zero because the sign representation does not occur in $V^{\otimes3}$ (equivalently $\Lambda^3V=0$), so the kernel is the sign block and the image is the corner of the other two blocks. The dimension count and the corner identification verify the general statement of the preceding Definition in the smallest non-stable case.
